text: Chapter 4's dependency conditions chained activities together inside one single pipeline. Trigger dependencies do that same real job one level up, between tumbling window triggers — Trigger A only fires once Trigger B's dependency window has genuinely succeeded. A tumbling window trigger can depend on up to five other triggers at once.

Trigger A's window can depend on Trigger B's window concurrently, with an offset of zero, or earlier, with a negative offset instead. A negative offset is genuinely the far more common real pattern — don't start today's aggregation until yesterday's ingestion has actually finished.

The dependency window's size doesn't have to match the trigger depending on it, either — a daily trigger can depend on a full seven-day rolling window from a weekly aggregation instead. And a trigger can even depend on its own earlier runs, a self-dependency, keeping strictly sequential processing — self-dependency always requires a negative offset, the one case where it's mandatory rather than optional.

Monitor the whole chain under Monitoring, Trigger Runs — a trigger with real dependencies shows a hyperlink into a dedicated dependency view, and the Gantt view visualizes the entire chain at a single glance. Blue for pending or running, green once every dependent window has succeeded, red the moment one genuinely fails.

A tumbling window trigger waits on its dependencies for up to seven full days before timing out, and if one fails, you genuinely have to rerun it successfully before the dependent trigger can proceed — there's no automatic skip. Chapter 6 complete. Next, Chapter 7: Integration Runtimes — the real compute underneath every single activity this course has built so far.
